Northcott's Game

Game StrategyAlgorithms
Game: Every row has one white and one black checker. You take turns with the computer sliding a checker along its row, and whoever cannot move loses. You are white and go first.
How to play: Press one of your white checkers, then press a square in its row to slide it there. You may not jump over the black checker.

Look for the math

The pieces have two colours, so it looks as if each player has different moves, which would make it a more complicated kind of game. It is in fact an old friend wearing a disguise.

Nim in disguise

In each row count the empty squares between the two checkers: that is a heap of beans. Sliding your checker toward the other one takes beans off the heap, exactly as in Nim. Sliding it away puts beans back, which Nim does not allow. But whoever moves next can slide their own checker the same distance toward it and take them off again, so the heap is the same as before and the other player faces the same position. A move like this is called reversible, and a game with such moves is a bogus Nim.

Who wins

As in Nim, the player about to move loses exactly when the nim-sum (the bitwise XOR) of the heaps is 0. The computer plays this way: if the nim-sum is not 0 it reduces a heap to make it 0, and if it is 0 it takes a few beans at random and hopes. The test solved the whole game on every position of boards up to 7 squares wide and 3 rows tall, including the moves that add beans, and found no position left undecided and no exception to the rule. It also let the computer play thousands of games on full-size boards: from a start with nim-sum 0 it never lost, and a player who always makes the nim-sum 0 never lost against it from any other start. The button "Show a good move" gives you that move.

Why the game ends

Each time a player adds beans the opponent can take them away again, and the beans you could add keep shrinking toward the walls, so the game cannot go on forever. If you let both players move checkers of either colour, the game would never have to end.

Press "Show a good move" when the board is new. If it says there is none, the computer is the one in the winning seat: just play on and hope it slips.
